corrected_value.title: Habituation and dishabituation to speech and office noise.

decisions.location: Experiment 1, Discussion (lines 756-767); see also Experiment 1 introduction (lines 392-440, 495-528), Results (lines 674-702), and References (lines 1557-1559)
decisions.quote:
The results from this study support
the findings from Banbury and Berry[14] showing that office

noise can disrupt performance on working memory tasks (i.e.

mental arithmetic) but that this disruption can be habituated

to after a period of time in noise. This study has gone on

to show that participants fully habituated to the office noise

following 10 minutes intervening exposure.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. In Experiment 1 (N = 36 undergraduates), Smith, Waters, and Jones empirically retest the laboratory finding of Banbury and Berry (1997, ref. 14) that background office noise with speech initially disrupts cognitive task performance and that prior exposure to office noise produces habituation that removes this disruption (testing 5-minute habituation blocks up to 20 minutes). Experiment 1 finds a significant noise condition by habituation block interaction (F(8,132) = 4, p < 0.05) with initial impairment in office noise eliminated after 10 minutes of prior exposure, and the Discussion explicitly compares these results to Banbury and Berry [14]. Reference 14 in the bibliography (lines 1557-1559) provides the exact identity: 'Banbury S, Berry DC. Habituation and dishabituation to speech and office noise. J Exp Psychol Appl 1997;3:181-95.' with no DOI printed in the source text. The only shipped row for this work is input_row_index 665 (10.1038/365611a0, Rauscher, Shaw, & Ky, 1993, 'Music and spatial task performance', Nature, 365, 611), which is the Mozart effect original tested in Experiment 2 (sibling target_index 1), and sibling target_index 2 is Thompson et al. (2001). Because Banbury and Berry (1997) is an independent study by different authors on office-noise habituation, report equivalence does not apply and it is genuinely absent from all shipped rows.
